questions.text: What distinguishes application-level semantic response caching from exact response caching?

options.A: Semantic caching retrains model weights, whereas exact caching changes the prompt.
options.B: Semantic caching matches every query to the most recent response regardless of meaning.
options.C: Semantic caching reuses responses for sufficiently similar queries, while exact caching matches a request key.
options.D: Semantic caching only stores prompt prefixes, while exact caching only stores embeddings.

questions.explanation: Semantic response caching uses a similarity threshold to match queries, while exact caching looks up an identical request key.

questions.text: An application logs a stop alert when spending reaches its limit but continues making paid model calls. What change makes the spending limit enforceable?

options.A: Add a longer alert message after each additional paid call.
options.B: Record the same spending under a different model name.
options.C: Lower response temperature while leaving all requests admitted.
options.D: Check budget state before paid calls and reject or serve cached responses when stopped.

questions.explanation: A spending control must affect request admission before the paid call; merely recording an alert does not stop spending.

questions.text: ExactCache hashes model, messages, and temperature together. A response is stored with model="gpt-4o-mini", but lookup uses model="gpt-4o" with identical messages and temperature=0.0. Both models are uncached beforehand. What happens?

options.A: A cache miss, because changing the model changes the request key.
options.B: A cache hit, because the model is ignored when messages match.
options.C: A cache hit, because temperature=0.0 makes all models equivalent.
options.D: A TypeError, because two model names cannot share one cache.

questions.explanation: The model is part of the hashed key. The different lookup model produces a different key even with matching messages and temperature.
